version.changelog:
group-tour v3.2.0

- Expanded skill scope: now supports flight booking, hotel reservation, train tickets, attractions, visa info, insurance, car rental, and more, all via Fliggy (Alibaba Group).
- Added detailed CLI parameter tables for flights, hotels, and POIs; refined sort/filter options.
- Improved output formatting rules and validation steps for consistent, bookable results.
- Updated activation triggers and scenario playbooks (e.g., luxury/senior group tours).
- Critical execution rules clarified: must install/use flyai-cli and never answer from knowledge/training data.

llm.summary: The skill's behavior mostly matches its travel-search description, but it requires installing a third-party CLI from npm and instructs agents to write local execution logs and strictly rely on CLI output — these practices raise privacy/persistence and supply-chain questions you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (finding group tours via Fliggy/flyai) aligns with the instructions: all core operations are calls to the flyai CLI (search/keyword-search/search-hotel/etc.). No unrelated credentials, binaries, or capabilities are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tightly constrains answers to CLI outputs only and lists concrete CLI commands/parameters. That is coherent, but several runtime rules broaden scope: (1) a strict 'Self-test' requiring re-execution if booking links are missing could cause repeated CLI calls; (2) runbook suggests persisting an execution log (.flyai-execution-log.json) containing user_query and CLI results if filesystem writes are available. Persisting full request/response data can include PII or booking-sensitive info — the skill never clarifies redaction/retention policies.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec in registry (instruction-only), but SKILL.md mandates 'npm i -g @fly-ai/flyai-cli' when flyai isn't present. Installing a global npm package from the public registry is a moderate supply-chain risk: verify the package publisher and source repository before installing. The skill does not embed or fetch code from obscure URLs, but the npm package itself is an external dependency.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables or credentials, which is proportionate. One caveat: the flyai CLI or downstream booking flows may prompt for credentials or use local auth tokens — the skill doesn't mention or manage that. The runbook's suggested log writes could capture sensitive data returned by the CLI.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and autonomous invocation are normal. However, the runbook explicitly instructs creating and appending to a local .flyai-execution-log.json if filesystem writes are available. That means the skill can cause persistent local storage of user queries, parameters, and CLI results. Users should consider whether they want those artifacts and where they are stored.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing: 1) Verify the npm package @fly-ai/flyai-cli (publisher, npm page, GitHub repo, recent releases) since the skill depends on it; don't blindly run a global npm install. 2) Be aware the skill runs shell CLI commands (flyai ...) and may prompt for or use any credentials the flyai CLI requires — confirm how that CLI handles auth. 3) The skill's runbook suggests writing an execution log (.flyai-execution-log.json) containing requests and CLI outputs; if you care about privacy, decide whether to allow this file or inspect/redirect it. 4) The 'self-test' rule can cause repeated CLI executions if output doesn't match the template — expect extra network calls. 5) If you cannot trust or audit the flyai CLI, prefer running the CLI manually yourself and not granting an agent the ability to install packages or write files. If you want, provide the flyai CLI output manually instead of letting the agent install/run it.
